description: Probe queries used to manually inspect retrieval quality after the Day 2 ingest. Each entry captures the observed top hit and a failure-mode tag pointing at which technique would actually fix it. Used as the seed eval set for the Day 10 RAGAS run.

queries.notes: Single-entity definitional query. Top 3 all from the Gandalf article. Baseline retrieval handles this cleanly.

Answer 'Bard' appears in all three retrieved chunks but never as the top result's title. Multi-hop: 'Smaug' -> 'killed by' -> 'Bard'. Dense retrieval on the query pulls Smaug-centric chunks. A reranker cannot fix this because Bard's own article is not in the candidate set; the recall is the problem. Candidate for HyDE or query decomposition on Day 8.

queries.query: What rings did the Dwarves get?
queries.notes: Both sources' Dwarves articles surfaced. Cross-source consensus on factual queries is a positive signal.

queries.query: Tell me about the Battle of Five Armies
queries.notes: Correct article retrieved, but the chunk leads with Fandom maintenance template text ('The descriptive majority of this article's text is unsourced...'). FANDOM_STRIP_SELECTORS in fetch.py needs to also drop .notice / .ambox / .mbox. Day 2.5 cleanup.

Top 2 are correct Lúthien chunks. Third chunk is Edith Tolkien's gravestone inscription ('LUTHIEN 1889-1971'). Semantically related but wrong-context. A cross-encoder reranker would see the query expects 'Beren AND Lúthien together' and demote the chunk that only matches one name. Day 7 territory.

All three results from Wikipedia's Mithril article. Definitional 'what is X?' queries naturally favor Wikipedia's encyclopedic prose over Fandom's narrative style. Source-quality observation, not a bug. Source-weighted routing is a Day 11+ exploration if we ever care.

Bombadil's own dedicated article was not the top hit; we got the generic 'Middle-earth peoples' page that mentions him in a subsection. Likely the Bombadil article has lower keyword density of his own name relative to disambiguating context, so dense-only retrieval misses the keyword signal. Poster child for hybrid BM25 + dense retrieval on Day 6. Re-run this exact query after that change.
